deathCause.detail: Frederick II died at Castel Fiorentino in Apulia on 13 December 1250, traditionally recorded as from dysentery.

events.label: A Count Frederick may be identifiable in a 1053 royal charter
events.labelCn: 1053年的王室文书中可能出现可与他认同的腓特烈伯爵
events.note: A Count Frederick appears in a 1053 royal charter in Swabia, but identification with Frederick of Büren is plausible rather than secure; later Staufer genealogy is reconstructed from sparse evidence.

sourceNote: Wibald of Stavelot's Tabula Consanguinitatis as the central medieval genealogical witness; Otto of Freising, Gesta Friderici; John B. Freed, Frederick Barbarossa: The Prince and the Myth; Deutsche Biographie's Staufer family overview; Wikipedia only as a navigation aid.
notes:
Frederick of Büren is a reconstructed early ancestor of the Staufer rather than a well-documented territorial prince. His historical importance lies chiefly in fathering Frederick I, the first Hohenstaufen Duke of Swabia.

Confidence / caveats: The epithet 'of Büren', his dates, parentage, exact county, and the identification of a 1053 Count Frederick with this genealogical figure are all uncertain. Later genealogy, especially Wibald's twelfth-century table, is doing much of the evidentiary work. For that reason no birth/death year is supplied and the rating is kept below 5 rather than manufacturing events from conjecture.

fullName: Frederick I of Staufen, Duke of Swabia
displayNameCn: 士瓦本公爵腓特烈一世
fullNameCn: 霍亨斯陶芬的腓特烈一世，士瓦本公爵

events.label: Received the Duchy of Swabia from Henry IV
events.labelCn: 从亨利四世手中获授士瓦本公国
events.note: Henry IV elevated Frederick to the Duchy of Swabia during the civil war against the anti-king Rudolf of Rheinfelden, inaugurating Hohenstaufen ducal rule.

events.label: Was betrothed to Henry IV's daughter Agnes
events.labelCn: 与亨利四世之女阿格尼丝订婚
events.note: The betrothal to Agnes of Waiblingen tied Frederick and the Staufer directly to Henry IV's Salian imperial house.

events.label: Married Agnes of Waiblingen
events.labelCn: 与瓦伊布林根的阿格尼丝结婚
events.note: The marriage consolidated the dynastic alliance between the Hohenstaufen dukes of Swabia and the Salian imperial family.

events.label: Reached a settlement with Berthold of Zähringen over Swabia
events.labelCn: 与策林根的贝特霍尔德就士瓦本争端达成和解
events.note: The settlement with Berthold of Zähringen stabilized Frederick's possession of Swabia while allowing the rival Zähringen line to retain ducal status and important rights.

events.label: Established Lorch as a major Staufer dynastic monastery
events.labelCn: 确立洛尔希修道院为霍亨斯陶芬家族的重要宗教中心
events.note: Around 1100, Lorch Abbey became the principal Staufer dynastic burial and religious foundation; the exact foundation chronology is not perfectly fixed.

events.label: Tried to mediate between Henry IV and the rebellious Henry V
events.labelCn: 试图调停亨利四世与反叛的亨利五世
events.note: Late in his life Frederick remained closely tied to the Salian house and attempted mediation between Henry IV and his rebellious son Henry V.

events.label: Died, leaving Swabia to Frederick II
events.labelCn: 去世，士瓦本公国由腓特烈二世继承
events.note: Frederick was dead by July 1105, after which his son Frederick II succeeded to the Duchy of Swabia; no securely established exact death date or medical cause is used here.

sourceNote: Neue Deutsche Biographie, 'Friedrich I. von Schwaben'; Allgemeine Deutsche Biographie; German imperial regesta for Henry IV and Henry V; John B. Freed, Frederick Barbarossa: The Prince and the Myth.
notes:
Frederick I was the first Hohenstaufen Duke of Swabia. His investiture and marriage to the Salian princess Agnes transformed a regional Swabian comital family into a royal-dynastic contender.

Confidence / caveats: Birth c.1050 is approximate. His mother's ancestry is presented with varying labels in older scholarship, though Hildegard of the Egisheim-Mömpelgard milieu is standard. The exact date of Lorch Abbey's foundation and his exact death date remain uncertain; he was dead before 21 July 1105.

Unlinked family (not in roster): mother: Hildegard of Egisheim; child: Gertrude of Staufen

fullName: Frederick II of Staufen, Duke of Swabia
displayNameCn: 士瓦本公爵腓特烈二世
fullNameCn: 霍亨斯陶芬的腓特烈二世，士瓦本公爵

events.label: Succeeded his father as Duke of Swabia
events.labelCn: 继承父亲成为士瓦本公爵
events.note: Frederick succeeded his father Frederick I as Duke of Swabia, preserving the Staufer ducal position through the final years of the Salian dynasty.

events.label: Accompanied Henry V's Italian expedition
events.labelCn: 随亨利五世参加意大利远征
events.note: Frederick accompanied Henry V into Italy and remained an important military and political supporter of his Salian uncle.

events.label: Acted as an imperial regent in Germany during Henry V's absence
events.labelCn: 亨利五世离境期间在德意志承担帝国摄政职责
events.note: Frederick and his brother Conrad exercised royal authority in Germany while Henry V campaigned in Italy.

events.label: Married Judith of Bavaria of the Welf house
events.labelCn: 与韦尔夫家族的巴伐利亚尤迪特结婚
events.note: The marriage to Judith of Bavaria connected the Hohenstaufen and Welf houses; the exact wedding year is not securely fixed and is usually reconstructed between 1119 and 1121.

events.label: Contested the German royal succession after Henry V's death
events.labelCn: 亨利五世去世后争夺德意志王位
events.note: Frederick's claim to the German throne, strengthened by Salian descent through his mother, was rejected in favor of Lothair of Supplinburg.

events.label: Joined the Hohenstaufen rebellion as Conrad was elected rival king
events.labelCn: 弟弟康拉德被拥立为对立国王后参加霍亨斯陶芬叛乱
events.note: Frederick and his brother Conrad resisted King Lothair III's attempt to recover former Salian imperial property from the Hohenstaufen.

events.label: Submitted to Lothair III and ended the civil conflict
events.labelCn: 向洛泰尔三世臣服，结束内战
events.note: The reconciliation with Lothair III in 1135–1136 restored the Hohenstaufen to the political community and preserved their dynastic position.

events.label: Died at Alzey
events.labelCn: 在阿尔蔡去世
events.note: Frederick II died at Alzey after more than four decades as Duke of Swabia.

sourceNote: Neue Deutsche Biographie, 'Friedrich II. von Schwaben'; Deutsche Biographie Staufer family overview; German imperial regesta for Henry V and Lothair III; John B. Freed, Frederick Barbarossa: The Prince and the Myth.
notes:
Frederick II inherited Swabia and the Salian dynastic claim transmitted through his mother Agnes of Waiblingen. His failed bid in the 1125 royal election was followed by a long Staufer-Lothair conflict, but his son Frederick Barbarossa later converted that dynastic capital into the imperial crown.

Confidence / caveats: Birth c.1090 is approximate. The marriage to Judith of Bavaria is generally placed between 1119 and 1121; the 1120 event is an explicit approximate placement, not a claimed exact date. The exact scope and terminology of his 1116–1118 regency varies in scholarship.

deathPlaceCn: 西西里王国马尔蒂拉诺
primaryTitle: King of Germany (King of the Romans)
primaryTitleCn: 德意志国王（罗马人的国王）

titles.title: King of Germany (King of the Romans)
titles.titleCn: 德意志国王（罗马人的国王）

events.label: Was crowned child King of Sicily
events.labelCn: 幼年加冕西西里国王
events.note: Frederick II used his son Henry's Sicilian kingship as part of the arrangements surrounding his own move north for the German crown.

events.label: Was brought to Germany and made Duke of Swabia
events.labelCn: 被带往德意志并成为士瓦本公爵
events.note: Henry was brought from Sicily into the German political sphere and received the Duchy of Swabia.

events.label: Was elected King of Germany at Frankfurt
events.labelCn: 在法兰克福被选为德意志国王
events.note: Henry's election at Frankfurt secured a Hohenstaufen succession in Germany while Frederick II prepared for imperial coronation.

events.label: Was crowned King at Aachen
events.labelCn: 在亚琛加冕为德意志国王
events.note: Henry received the German royal coronation at Aachen.

events.label: Married Margaret of Austria
events.labelCn: 与奥地利的玛格丽特结婚
events.note: The marriage joined Henry to Margaret of Austria of the Babenberg dynasty.

events.label: Openly resisted Frederick II and sought a princely alliance
events.labelCn: 公开反抗腓特烈二世并寻求诸侯联盟
events.note: Long-running disputes over royal policy in Germany turned into open rebellion by Henry against his father Frederick II, with Henry seeking support among German princes.

events.label: Was forced to submit and lost the German kingship
events.labelCn: 被迫向腓特烈二世臣服并失去德意志王位
events.note: Frederick II crushed Henry's rebellion, forced his submission, deprived him of royal dignity and placed him under arrest.

events.label: Was transferred into long-term captivity in southern Italy
events.labelCn: 被转移到南意大利长期囚禁
events.note: Henry was held at a succession of fortified sites in Apulia and Calabria, far from his former German power base.

events.label: Died after a fall during a prison transfer near Martirano
events.labelCn: 在马尔蒂拉诺附近囚禁转移途中坠落后死亡
events.note: Henry died after a fall during a prison transfer near Martirano. Medieval sources often interpreted the fall as deliberate suicide, but the intention cannot be established with certainty.

sourceNote: Neue Deutsche Biographie, 'Heinrich (VII.)'; Wolfgang Stürner, Friedrich II.; David Abulafia, Frederick II: A Medieval Emperor; German royal regesta; paleopathological work on Henry's remains used only for contextual caution.
notes:
Henry (VII) was Frederick II's son and subordinate German king, not the later Emperor Henry VII of Luxembourg. His rebellion and deposition in 1235 made him a failed Hohenstaufen co-monarch whose sons never recovered the royal position.

Confidence / caveats: The parentheses in Henry (VII) are historiographically important: he was king but never emperor and is conventionally excluded from the imperial numbering sequence that later produced Emperor Henry VII. His election was in 1220 while his Aachen coronation followed in 1222, so sources sometimes start his royal 'reign' at different points. His 1242 fall is factual; whether it was an accident or deliberate suicide remains uncertain. Some forensic work has argued he suffered from leprosy, but this is not used as a death cause.

deathCause.summary: Died from injuries after a fall while in captivity
deathCause.summaryCn: 囚禁转移途中坠落后因伤去世
deathCause.detail: Henry died after a fall during a prison transfer near Martirano. Medieval sources often interpreted the fall as deliberate suicide, but the intention cannot be established with certainty.
deathCause.detailCn: 在马尔蒂拉诺附近囚禁转移途中坠落后死亡。中世纪史料常将其解读为自杀，但意图无法确定。

events.label: Married Beatrice of Savoy
events.labelCn: 与萨伏依的贝阿特丽丝结婚
events.note: The marriage joined Manfred of the Hohenstaufen to Beatrice of Savoy.

events.label: Inherited the Principality of Taranto and a major role in Sicilian government
events.labelCn: 继承塔兰托亲王领并在西西里政府中取得重要地位
events.note: Frederick II's death left Manfred as Prince of Taranto and the strongest resident Hohenstaufen prince in southern Italy while Conrad IV remained the senior heir.

events.label: Became regent in Sicily for the infant Conradin after Conrad IV's death
events.labelCn: 康拉德四世去世后为幼年康拉丁摄政
events.note: After Conrad IV's death, Manfred became regent in Sicily for the infant Conradin; the regency quickly became entangled in open conflict with the papacy.

events.label: Was crowned King of Sicily
events.labelCn: 加冕西西里国王
events.note: Manfred was crowned at Palermo after reports that Conradin had died; when those reports proved false, he did not surrender the Sicilian crown.

events.label: Married Helena Angelina Doukaina
events.labelCn: 与海伦娜·安格丽娜·杜凯娜结婚
events.note: The marriage to Helena Angelina Doukaina strengthened Manfred's Adriatic and Epirote connections.

events.label: His Sicilian troops helped the Ghibellines win at Montaperti
events.labelCn: 其西西里军队帮助吉伯林派赢得蒙塔佩尔蒂战役
events.note: At the Battle of Montaperti, Sicilian troops supplied by Manfred helped the Ghibelline coalition win, greatly expanding his influence in central and northern Italian politics.

events.label: Faced the Angevin invasion sanctioned by the papacy
events.labelCn: 面对教宗支持的安茹的查理入侵
events.note: Papal transfer of the Sicilian crown to Charles of Anjou led to an Angevin invasion of Manfred's kingdom and turned the papal-Hohenstaufen conflict into a decisive military campaign.

events.label: Was defeated and killed at the Battle of Benevento
events.labelCn: 在贝内文托战役中战败并阵亡
events.note: At the Battle of Benevento, Manfred was defeated and killed by the forces of Charles of Anjou. His death ended Hohenstaufen rule in the kingdom in practice, although Conradin remained the dynastic claimant.

sourceNote: Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani/Treccani, 'Manfredi, re di Sicilia'; David Abulafia, The Western Mediterranean Kingdoms; Steven Runciman, The Sicilian Vespers; Wolfgang Stürner and Hohenstaufen scholarship; contemporary southern Italian chronicles treated critically.
notes:
Manfred converted a regency for his nephew Conradin into his own kingship in 1258. His defeat and death at Benevento transferred effective control of Sicily to Charles of Anjou and set up Conradin's final failed restoration attempt.

Confidence / caveats: Manfred's legitimacy was politically contested because his parents' marital status at his birth is uncertain; later Hohenstaufen-friendly tradition emphasized a late marriage and legitimation. His kingship from 1258 was effective in Sicily but disputed by the papacy and by Conradin's hereditary claim. The family list includes the principal attested children; medieval and modern genealogies vary in naming some of the children from his second marriage.

birthPlaceCn: 兰茨胡特附近沃尔夫施泰因城堡
primaryTitle: Duke of Swabia and claimant King of Sicily
primaryTitleCn: 士瓦本公爵兼西西里王位宣称者

titles.title: King of Jerusalem (de jure claimant)
titles.titleCn: 耶路撒冷国王（法理宣称）

titles.title: King of Sicily (Hohenstaufen claimant)
titles.titleCn: 西西里国王（霍亨斯陶芬宣称）

events.label: Inherited his father's Hohenstaufen claims as a two-year-old
events.labelCn: 两岁时继承父亲的霍亨斯陶芬王位宣称
events.note: After Conrad IV's death, the two-year-old Conradin inherited Hohenstaufen claims to Sicily and Jerusalem under guardianship, but possessed neither kingdom in effective personal rule.

events.label: Manfred had himself crowned King of Sicily despite Conradin's hereditary claim
events.labelCn: 曼弗雷德无视康拉丁的世袭权利自行加冕西西里国王
events.note: Manfred was crowned King of Sicily at Palermo after a false report of Conradin's death and retained the crown even after learning that Conradin was alive.

events.label: Formally took possession of the Duchy of Swabia
events.labelCn: 正式取得士瓦本公国
events.note: At Ulm, Conradin appeared formally as Duke of Swabia, making 1262 a safer start for the ducal title than retroactively dating it to infancy.

events.label: Was invited by Italian Ghibellines to reclaim the Hohenstaufen inheritance after Manfred's death
events.labelCn: 曼弗雷德战死后受意大利吉伯林派邀请收复霍亨斯陶芬遗产
events.note: After Manfred's death, Italian Ghibellines invited Conradin to reclaim the Hohenstaufen inheritance from Charles of Anjou, launching the final restoration attempt.

events.label: Crossed the Alps on his Italian expedition
events.labelCn: 率军翻越阿尔卑斯山展开意大利远征
events.note: Conradin crossed the Alps with his supporters as part of the campaign to recover the Hohenstaufen inheritance in Italy.

events.label: Was excommunicated during the campaign against Charles of Anjou
events.labelCn: 在反对安茹的查理的远征中遭绝罚
events.note: Conradin was excommunicated by the papacy during his campaign against Charles of Anjou.

events.label: Entered Rome to an enthusiastic Ghibelline reception
events.labelCn: 进入罗马并受到吉伯林派热烈欢迎
events.note: Conradin entered Rome and received an enthusiastic welcome from the city's Ghibelline supporters.

events.label: Was defeated by Charles of Anjou at Tagliacozzo
events.labelCn: 在塔利亚科佐战役中被安茹的查理击败
events.note: At the Battle of Tagliacozzo, Conradin's forces were defeated by Charles of Anjou.

events.label: Was captured while trying to escape from Italy
events.labelCn: 试图逃离意大利时被俘
events.note: Conradin was captured near Torre Astura while attempting to escape from Italy after his defeat.

events.label: Was publicly beheaded at Naples
events.labelCn: 在那不勒斯被公开斩首
events.note: Conradin was publicly executed by beheading at Naples under Charles of Anjou. His death ended the legitimate male Hohenstaufen line and became a potent symbol of the Angevin conquest of southern Italy.

sourceNote: Neue Deutsche Biographie, 'Konradin'; Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani/Treccani, 'Corradino'; David Abulafia, The Western Mediterranean Kingdoms; Steven Runciman, The Sicilian Vespers; contemporary Italian and German chronicles treated critically.
notes:
Conradin was the last legitimate male Hohenstaufen and the hereditary rival to both Manfred's self-coronation and Charles of Anjou's papally sponsored conquest. His 1268 defeat and execution ended any realistic Hohenstaufen restoration in Sicily and Swabia.

Confidence / caveats: His numbering varies by title: he can appear as Conrad II of Swabia, Conrad V in some dynastic royal sequences, and most commonly simply Conradin/Konradin. His Sicilian and Jerusalem titles were overwhelmingly de jure claims after 1254 rather than effective rule. The ducal start is set to 1262 because Deutsche Biographie identifies the Ulm assumption of the duchy then, although some genealogies retroactively style him duke from 1254. The 1266 proxy marriage to Sophia of Landsberg was never followed by normal married cohabitation and may never have been consummated.
